sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let's explore how to hide the messy details of your code while keeping it powerful and easy to use!

• What class abstraction and encapsulation really mean
• How to protect your data like a pro
• Why these concepts make your code cleaner and safer

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine a coffee machine. You press a button and get coffee - you don't need to know how the beans are ground or how the water is heated. That's abstraction!

**Abstraction** hides complex details while showing only what's necessary.

• Think of a car's steering wheel - you don't need to know how the engine works to drive
• In code, abstraction means exposing simple methods while hiding complex logic

**Encapsulation** is like putting your data in a protective capsule.

• It bundles data and methods that work on that data
• It restricts direct access to some components (like private variables)
• It prevents accidental modification of important data

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Class Abstraction and Encapsulation works:

steps.title: The Problem
steps.description: Without encapsulation, anyone can mess with your data directly.

steps.title: Adding Encapsulation
steps.description: Protect the data by making it private and adding controlled access.

steps.title: Using Abstraction
steps.description: Now users only see simple methods, not the internal workings.

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ Abstraction = Show only what's necessary, hide the rest
✓ Encapsulation = Protect your data like a treasure chest
✓ Use private fields with public getters/setters
✓ Methods should do one thing well (Single Responsibility)

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Keep methods focused on one task
Use clear method names that describe what they do
donts: Don't create 'god objects' that do everything
Don't make getters that return mutable objects directly
sections.protip: When designing a class, ask: 'What should users of this class NOT need to know?' - that's what to abstract away!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Class Abstraction and Encapsulation used in real apps?

examples.how: You interact with simple buttons (abstraction) while your account data is protected (encapsulation)
You post content through simple methods while the platform handles all the complex storage and distribution
Character classes expose simple move() methods while handling complex physics and collision detection internally

problem.description: Create a Temperature class that stores temperature in Celsius but provides methods to get/set in both Celsius and Fahrenheit. The internal storage should remain in Celsius only.
hints: Make sure to validate temperature values
Think about what methods users would need
problem.explanation: This solution encapsulates the celsius field while providing a clean interface for both temperature scales. Users don't need to know the internal storage format.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Encapsulation = Protect your data like a fortress
📌 Always use private fields with public methods
📌 You're now ready to design cleaner, safer classes!
